skill.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skill.description: Set up repository configuration files for Matt Pocock engineering skills, including issue tracker rules, triage labels, and domain documentation guidance.
skill.summary: Scaffolds repo guidance that Matt Pocock engineering skills read before planning, triage, and architecture work.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static shell-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans and fenced examples in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby or shell interpolation. The skill is prompt-driven and requires user confirmation before writing setup docs, but it does intentionally edit persistent agent guidance files. No prompt injection text or hidden data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Continue showing exact drafts before editing CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or docs/agents files. Require explicit user approval before each write.
Clearly state when GitHub or GitLab CLI actions may create, label, comment on, or close remote issues. Ask before any authenticated write.
Where possible, describe file names and labels without ambiguous inline command formatting, or document that examples are prose only.

semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the assistant to update CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and write docs/agents files after showing drafts. This is intended setup behavior, but it persists instructions that future agents may read.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly requires drafting an Agent skills block, choosing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, and writing docs/agents files. The workflow also requires user review before writing, so the risk is limited.

content.value_statement: Engineering skills need shared repo rules before they can triage issues or read domain context safely. This skill records issue tracker, label, and domain documentation choices for future agent sessions.
actual_capabilities: Inspects repository setup markers such as git remotes, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT files, ADR folders, and .scratch.
Guides issue tracker selection across GitHub, GitLab, local markdown, or a user-defined workflow.
Maps five canonical triage states to the label names used by the repository.
Drafts an Agent skills section for the existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md file.
Creates docs/agents guidance files for issue tracking, triage labels, and domain documentation layout.
limitations: It is a prompt-driven setup workflow, not a deterministic installer script.
It does not create remote labels or issue tracker settings by itself.
It needs user input when no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md file exists.
It records conventions for other skills, but it does not enforce them automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare a solo repository
use_cases.description: Set up local markdown issue tracking and default triage labels before using planning or triage skills.

use_cases.title: Standardize open-source triage
use_cases.description: Document whether GitHub or GitLab issues and external pull requests should enter the triage workflow.

use_cases.title: Align architecture context
use_cases.description: Record whether the repo uses one domain context or multiple contexts with ADRs for each area.

prompt_templates.title: Start Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository without established agent guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up this repository for Matt Pocock engineering skills. Inspect existing repo guidance and ask each setup question one at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Use GitHub Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Configure a repository that tracks work in GitHub Issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure this repo for GitHub Issues. Preserve existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md content and show drafts before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Use Local Markdown
prompt_templates.scenario: Configure a repo that does not use a remote issue tracker.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up local markdown issue tracking for this repo. Use default triage labels unless existing labels are already documented.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Existing Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced update for a repository that already has docs/agents guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit and update the existing setup. Preserve custom guidance, refresh docs/agents files, and explain every changed decision before editing.

output_examples.input: Set up a GitHub repository for the engineering skills.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the detected GitHub remote, proposes GitHub Issues, asks about external pull requests, then drafts the agent guidance files.

output_examples.input: Use local markdown issues for a small project.
output_examples.output: The skill records the .scratch workflow, keeps default triage states, and prepares docs that future skills can read.

output_examples.input: Update a repo that already has CLAUDE.md.
output_examples.output: The skill edits the existing agent guidance section in place, avoids duplicate sections, and writes supporting docs under docs/agents.

best_practices: Review every draft before allowing the skill to write persistent guidance files.
Choose the issue tracker that the team already uses for real work.
Keep label mappings aligned with actual tracker labels to avoid duplicate triage states.
anti_patterns: Do not run setup before deciding where the team tracks issues.
Do not create a second agent guidance file when one already exists.
Do not accept default labels if the tracker already uses different names.

faq.question: Does this skill run an installer script?
faq.answer: No. It is a guided setup workflow that asks questions, drafts changes, and writes files after approval.

faq.question: Which agent guidance file does it edit?
faq.answer: It edits CLAUDE.md if present, otherwise AGENTS.md. If neither exists, it asks which one to create.

faq.question: Can it use GitLab instead of GitHub?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports GitLab issue tracking and records GitLab-specific guidance when that option is selected.

faq.question: Does it create labels in the issue tracker?
faq.answer: No. It records the label names that other skills should use when they process issues.

faq.question: Why does it ask about domain documentation?
faq.answer: Other engineering skills read context files and ADRs to use the project language and respect architecture decisions.

faq.question: Can the setup be changed later?
faq.answer: Yes. Edit docs/agents files directly, or rerun the skill when changing issue trackers or domain layout.
